title: Rank task records for pre-edit delivery: gate by structure, score by a six-term convex sum with outcome weight, fill five slots (latest, violation, relevant×3) with a factual reason per line
context: 1.36.0 delivers the three most recent graph tasks that touched a file. Recency is not relevance: once a file has dozens of tasks, the one that matters (same rule, a violation, a failed check) falls off. David (2026-09-15) asked for the agent's context to drive selection and for 'last three plus most relevant'. A three-thread research pass (literature, products, IR practice; synthesis in the private overlay, finding recorded the same day) found: gating before ranking is what separates every reported win from every reported loss; structure/entity overlap beats embeddings; verified outcome is the only deterministic importance proxy with evidence; convex weighted sums beat RRF at small list sizes; superseded records must be excluded because models do not detect staleness; each injected line needs one data-backed reason; nobody ships per-file task history ranked by outcome.
decision: Replace 'three most recent' with: (1) GATE: candidates are tasks that touched the file, a dependent/same-component file, a co-changed file (≥2 non-bulk commits), or share a delivered rule with the current task; superseded records and records with no surviving file anchors are excluded. (2) SCORE, convex sum of terms in [0,1]: file 0.30 (same 1, dependent 0.5, co-change 0.3); rules 0.25 (IDF-weighted intersection of record ids with the current task's ledger); outcome 0.15 (violated 1, failed check 0.8, saved decision 0.6, rule-supported application 0.5, passed check 0.3); lexical 0.10 (FTS5 bm25 of the current task title or hunch_context phrase over task and lesson titles, normalized to the top hit); recency 0.10 (0.5^(days/30), floor 0.1, on last delivery else finished_at); working set 0.10 (overlap with files this task already touched). Ties: newest, then id. (3) SLOTS, max five: latest task on the exact file; most recent violation or failed check in scope; three top scores with MMR λ=0.7 over files ∪ rule ids. (4) PRESENTATION: one factual reason per line in slot vocabulary, verbatim ids and dates, 'files since changed' when anchors moved, header with the count of more. Intent when titles are opted out comes from the task's own ledger; no prompt text retained. (5) EVALUATION pre-registered: offline leave-one-out Hit@5/MRR against all records with temporal split and paired bootstrap CIs; online re-verification and repeat-violation rates from task records; interleaving to compare rankers; kill rule: if Hit@5 does not beat 'latest 3 by file' with a CI-backed margin after 200 tasks, ship latest-only. Weights change only through that metric.
consequences: Ranking is deterministic and replayable; every line carries its reason; superseded records never appear.
New inputs: co-change from git log, dependents from the symbol graph, last-delivery time from receipts; all local.
The first shipped version is a hypothesis until the leave-one-out number exists; the kill rule is part of the decision.
alternatives_rejected: Keep 'three most recent': recency ranks the loud file over the relevant task; the literature's negative results are all unfiltered injection.

LLM reranker or LLM-rated importance: forbidden by the subscription-CLI rule, non-replayable, mixed evidence (SWE-Exp +3.8 vs Memory Transfer Learning negative), no evidence that rated importance helps agents.

Embeddings as the primary relevance signal: structure/entity signals outperform them in Zep, HippoRAG, MemCoder and Memp; keep the optional local model as a possible seventh term only if the offline metric asks.
Reciprocal rank fusion: at list sizes under 20 with k=60 it degenerates to a vote count and discards magnitude.
Jaccard over rule ids: saturates on one shared id; IDF-weighted intersection instead.
Flat top-5 without slots: a guaranteed latest and a guaranteed violation slot are the two lines with the clearest value; MMR keeps the rest from being five near-duplicates.
